scope: Three authorized diagnostic calls between two owned accounts, covering pre-acceptance and observed signaling acceptance. These probes test TURN allocation and exact payload exchange; full WebRTC media and proxy transfer are outside their scope.

liveObservation.executionReportedBy: parent agent controlling the local diagnostic runner

acceptedSignalingFollowup.executionReportedBy: parent agent controlling the local diagnostic runner
acceptedSignalingFollowup.interpretation: The accept signal was observed by the caller without creating additional WebRTC allocations. This still did not verify a bidirectional nonce exchange. Signaling acceptance alone does not establish full media negotiation or all service-side forwarding eligibility conditions.

stunBindingFollowup.executionReportedBy: parent agent controlling the local diagnostic runner
stunBindingFollowup.interpretation: Using valid STUN Binding framing did not change the receive-and-verify timeout in this same-host setup. The probe did not perform authenticated ICE connectivity checks, nomination or DTLS and does not identify why either direction failed to verify.

sourceAudit.permissionOrdering: RelayConnInternal.create_perm awaits create_permissions and marks the permission permitted after the transaction returns. Both first sends complete before the fixed second send round starts.
sourceAudit.channelBindOrdering: Channel bind can still be pending. RelayConnInternal.send_to uses a SEND-INDICATION in that state, so delivery does not require the background channel bind to have completed.
sourceAudit.sendLength: The return length can describe the encoded TURN message. The probe checks exact nonce length, content and peer address on receipt instead.
sourceAudit.receiveOrdering: The two receive futures are joined. A timeout establishes that both receives did not complete together within the overall budget; it does not reveal which direction completed or prove that no datagram arrived.
sourceAudit.officialPreAcceptanceBehavior: onReceiveConfig creates the incoming peer connection and sends an offer before acceptance. This supports pre-acceptance connection setup but does not establish the backend's forwarding policy before acceptance.

interpretationLimits: The first probe ran before acceptance. The next two followed observed signaling acceptance without media negotiation. Service-side forwarding eligibility is not established by these states.
The third probe used a valid STUN Binding request with a random transaction ID and padding. It did not test authenticated ICE checks, nomination, a network outage or full media transport.
Both allocations originated on the same Windows host. This does not test two independent access networks or isolate service relay hairpin behavior.
The probe makes two fixed sends per direction. Datagram loss and time consumed by allocation cannot be excluded by this result.
The successful local TURN mock proves the probe's fixture path, not compatibility with every service policy or relay deployment.
localCleanupComplete describes local close operations. It is not acknowledgement that every remote allocation was deleted, especially after a cancelled operation.
The earlier accepted WebRTC call failed ICE. The pre-acceptance raw TURN timeout neither exonerates ICE nor establishes that both failures share one cause.
No provider-blocking, account-policy, billing, throughput or final root-cause conclusion follows from these probes.

asymmetricMediaTrial.topology: Two retained accounts on one Windows host

asymmetricMediaTelemetryFollowup.topology: Two retained accounts on one Windows host
asymmetricMediaTelemetryFollowup.interpretation: The client failed route verification even though one ICE pair succeeded and one was nominated. The saved diagnostics do not include the selected candidate type or which route verification stage rejected the path.

nextDiagnostic: Distinguish client selected-candidate validation from verifier scheduling and readiness races. Test across two independent networks with the separate Windows and Linux endpoints.
